Terminal guide

Ghostty terminfo on Omarchy

The compiled xterm-ghostty entry, installed package-manager style — so SSH servers stop erroring on unknown terminals.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 · independent editorial guide

Short answer

Install with omarchy pkg add ghostty-terminfo on the remote machine (not your laptop — Ghostty already bundles the entry locally). It lays down the xterm-ghostty terminfo entry so ncurses tools stop failing with 'unknown terminal' over SSH. Verify with infocmp xterm-ghostty. No root? Use the infocmp -x xterm-ghostty | ssh YOUR-SERVER -- tic -x - one-liner instead.

Ghostty Terminfo on Omarchy

Ghostty's compiled terminfo entries (xterm-ghostty) installed into the system database without the terminal itself — so SSH servers, containers, and any machine that never runs Ghostty's GUI can still understand TERM=xterm-ghostty instead of erroring.

TL;DR

omarchy pkg add ghostty-terminfo
# confirm it's there:
infocmp xterm-ghostty

Install it on the machine that must recognize Ghostty's terminal type (often a remote server, not your laptop). Takes under a minute.

Getting started (5 minutes)

1. Understand the problem this solves.

When you SSH from Ghostty, only the name in your TERM variable travels to the remote — the capability database that explains xterm-ghostty stays on your laptop. If the remote has no entry for it, ncurses tools blow up with tput: unknown terminal "xterm-ghostty", missing or unsuitable terminal: xterm-ghostty, or Error opening terminal: xterm-ghostty. — and WARNING: terminal is not fully functional. This package is the missing entry, installed the package-manager way. (Per Ghostty's terminfo docs.)

2. The three things everyone needs to know:

  • Install it where the error happens. Your laptop's Ghostty already has the entry locally — this package goes on the remote machine (or any Omarchy box that must resolve TERM=xterm-ghostty, e.g. a VM or container you SSH into). No laptop-side config changes needed.
  • Verify with one command. infocmp xterm-ghostty should print the entry; tput -T xterm-ghostty longname prints its description. If you get "unknown terminal" (exit code 3), the entry isn't installed where the command ran.
  • You won't need it forever. Ghostty's terminfo landed upstream in ncurses 6.5-20241228 (January 2025). As distros ship newer ncurses, the entry arrives system-wide by default — this package is the bridge until then. (Per the docs.)

3. Alternatives for machines you can't install packages on.

No root? The documented one-liner copies the entry over SSH using your laptop's Ghostty install — no package needed on the remote:

infocmp -x xterm-ghostty | ssh YOUR-SERVER -- tic -x -

Then check /usr/share/terminfo/... (or $HOME/.terminfo/...) on the server. Ignore tic's "older tic versions may treat the description field as an alias" warning. Or, if Ghostty 1.2+ on the laptop: shell-integration-features = ssh-terminfo in ~/.config/ghostty/config makes Ghostty install the entry automatically on first SSH. As a last resort, SetEnv TERM=xterm-256color in ~/.ssh/config (OpenSSH 8.7+) works everywhere but loses Ghostty-only features like colored/styled underlines.

Common issues & fixes

tput: unknown terminal "xterm-ghostty" over SSH, or missing or unsuitable terminal: xterm-ghostty in tmux on the remote

Fix: The remote lacks the entry — install this package on the remote (or run the infocmp | ssh tic one-liner above). The tmux case is the same root cause: tmux on the remote reads the remote's terminfo database, not your laptop's.

sudo htop fails with 'xterm-ghostty': unknown terminal type

Fix: sudo strips the TERMINFO env var (note: sudo -E alone doesn't fix it — /etc/sudoers must also allow the variable; that's from mitchellh's comment on the issue). Options: configure sudo to preserve TERMINFO, or enable Ghostty's sudo wrapper with shell-integration-features = sudo in your Ghostty config (off by default). Sourced from ghostty-org/ghostty#1291.

Your macOS laptop's infocmp spits Illegal character errors in the copy pipeline

Fix: macOS pre-Sonoma ships an ancient ncurses. brew install ncurses and use /opt/homebrew/opt/ncurses/bin/infocmp (Apple Silicon) in the one-liner. (Per Ghostty's terminfo docs.)

Ubuntu 24.04 server can't produce an xterm-ghostty entry at all

Fix: Its ncurses (6.4) predates the upstream entry — installing ncurses-term won't help. Copy the entry manually with the infocmp | ssh tic one-liner from your Ghostty machine; verify with tput -T xterm-ghostty longname (exit 3 = still unknown). Sourced from Ghostty's terminfo docs and a walkthrough of the Ubuntu case.

You set SetEnv TERM=xterm-256color for all hosts and now styled underlines are gone everywhere

Fix: Only apply that fallback stanza to hosts that actually lack the entry. On hosts where xterm-ghostty resolves, keep the full TERM to retain Ghostty-only capabilities. (Per Ghostty's SSH docs.)

Pairs well with

  • ghostty-shell-integration (Omarchy App Store — the shell scripts behind Ghostty's ssh-terminfo/ssh-env automation, installable without the GUI), ghostty itself (Omarchy App Store — already bundles the terminfo; you'd never install this split package on a box that runs Ghostty), and tmux (the other app most likely to hit the "unknown terminal" error on a remote box).

If you hate this, try

  • the SetEnv TERM=xterm-256color fallback in ~/.ssh/config — zero packages, works on any host, costs you Ghostty's extra capabilities. Or run the manual infocmp | ssh tic pipeline once per server and skip the package entirely.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need this on my laptop if I already run Ghostty?

No. Ghostty's own packages include the terminfo entry — the docs say Ghostty packages "include the terminfo entry and set the proper filesystem layouts." This package is for other machines (servers, containers, VMs) that never run Ghostty's GUI.

What TERM does Ghostty use, and why xterm-ghostty?

Ghostty sets TERM=xterm-ghostty. During private beta a bare ghostty value broke apps that string-match "xterm" in TERM, so upstream settled on the xterm- prefix for compatibility. (Ghostty's terminfo docs.)

Can I install it without root?

Yes. tic falls back to writing $HOME/.terminfo when it can't write /usr/share/terminfo — create the directory first. ncurses checks $HOME/.terminfo before system dirs unless $TERMINFO overrides. (Ghostty's terminfo docs.)

When will I stop needing this package?

When every box you touch ships ncurses ≥ 6.5-20241228, the entry is there by default. Per the docs: "as distros update their ncurses packages, Ghostty's terminfo entry will be available by default system-wide. This will take time to propagate."

Does the xterm-256color fallback lose anything?

Yes — Ghostty-only capabilities like colored and styled underlines. It's a safe universal fallback, not a feature-complete one.
